negotiation_summary: Atlas is negotiating dedicated capacity terms focused on throughput guarantees. They require a minimum sustained tokens/sec guarantee across a reserved pool, clear concurrency caps per API key/model, and an explicit burst policy (duration and billing). Pricing sensitivity is high — they compare to building an internal fleet. Legal wants explicit data residency & audit log retention in SLA. Sales proposed 12 reserved GPUs with automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants during saturation.
throughput_requirements: min_sustained_tokens_per_sec: 25,000 aggregate across reserved pool (measured p60 over 1 hour)
concurrency_cap_per_customer_api_key: 300 concurrent requests (soft limit), 400 (hard) with throttling/backpressure
per_model_concurrency_limit: 150 for flagship reranker model; 50 for experimental models
burst_policy_request: allow 3x sustained throughput for 10 minutes once per hour; additional bursts evaluated and billed separately
latency_target: p95 < 350ms for chat endpoints under guaranteed throughput; p99 < 900ms with failover behaviour
sla_terms_proposed: Throughput SLA: minimum tokens/sec as above, credit-based remediation if below for 3 consecutive windows
Latency SLA: p95 target thresholds; credits if p95 breached for >30 minutes aggregated per month
Capacity planning: Redwood to reserve 12x A100-equivalent capacity in NA with proactive scaling/burst plumbing
Fallback policy: automatic routing to lower-cost quantized variant when capacity exceeded; customer notified via webhook
